quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

60 Questions • Passing Score 50

questions.question: When driving on snow or ice, what should you do?

options.text: It is safe to use your cruise control.
Make changes to speed and direction slowly and gradually.
Drive the same way you would on normal roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make changes to speed and direction slowly and gradually.
questions.explanation: On snow or ice, slow down and turn gradually. Do not use cruise control on snow or ice. Your tires may slip and you could lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are also coming to the intersection.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop, let others pass, and go only when it is safe.

questions.question: When you approach a roundabout, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when entering a roundabout. Roundabouts are meant to be driven at low speeds.

questions.question: An aggressive driver cuts you off. What should you do?

options.text: Stay calm and move out of their way.
Flash your lights to show the driver they are wrong.
Do something to get back at the aggressive driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of their way.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and let the aggressive driver pass. Trying to get revenge makes the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Drive to the side shown by the arrow.
You can drive in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the side shown by the arrow.
questions.explanation: This is a "Keep right" sign. There is a traffic island, median, or barrier ahead. Drive to the right of it.

questions.question: You see a flashing yellow light at an intersection. What must you do?

options.text: Wait for a green light before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be careful. Watch for traffic and pedestrians crossing.

questions.question: This sign warns of what?
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert drivers. This sign warns that the road ends at an intersection ahead. Slow down and be ready to turn right or left or to stop.

questions.question: Drivers do not have to let pedestrians cross if they are walking against the traffic light. True or false?
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Always let pedestrians cross safely. Pedestrians may sometimes cross against the light, so stay alert.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign shows a pedestrian crossing area. Watch for people crossing the road and let them pass safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Side road.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a side road meets your road ahead.

questions.question: A solid red arrow on a traffic signal means:

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same thing as a red circle light.
You may turn in the direction the arrow points.
Traffic in that direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a red circle light.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red circle light. You must stop and cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: Two solid yellow lines on the road mean:

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed at the top of a hill.
Passing is allowed during the day only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mean traffic on the other side is moving toward you. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass from either direction.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
questions.correctAnswerText: Human error
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do not see other vehicles or do something unexpected. Talk to other drivers to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: As you drive faster, it is important to:

options.text: Look far ahead of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle needs more distance to stop at higher speeds. When driving fast, look far ahead so you have time to safely react to danger.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check your blind spots and mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal to alert other drivers. Check your mirrors and turn your head to check your blind spot before moving left or right.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign is:
questions.correctAnswerText: A warning sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow (or orange in work areas). They warn you of danger ahead or special rules.

questions.question: To reduce glare from headlights at night, you should look:

options.text: At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming drivers do not dim their lights, keep your eyes on the right edge of the road. Do not look at the headlights because the glare can blind you.

questions.question: Before stopping at a traffic signal or stop sign, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors for nearby traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors for nearby traffic.
questions.explanation: When stopping, check your mirrors first. Be aware of other drivers as you slow down. Then press the brake pedal smoothly to stop.

questions.question: To stay safe at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.
Listen, look both ways, and cross only if it is safe.
Cross quickly when a train is coming.
Quickly pass under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen, look both ways, and cross only if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions before crossing. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: Drivers must obey instructions from:

options.text: Other drivers whose vehicles have broken down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flaggers at construction sites.
questions.explanation: Drivers must obey flaggers at construction sites. They are there to keep drivers and workers safe.

questions.question: What shape is a stop sign?
questions.correctAnswerText: Octagon
questions.explanation: Only stop signs have an octagonal (eight-sided) shape. This shape tells drivers to come to a complete stop.

questions.question: Your right wheels leave the pavement. What should you do?

options.text: Pull completely off the road and get back on when safe.
Speed up and steer back onto the road quickly.
Release the accelerator, slow down, and ease back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator, slow down, and ease back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: If your right wheels leave the pavement, do not panic. Release the accelerator and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and ease back onto the road by keeping both hands on the wheel and making a small turn. Check for traffic before steering back onto the pavement.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Drive the same as you would on dry roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the space between your vehicle and the one ahead. Your vehicle will need more time to stop in these conditions.

questions.question: If you drive slower than other traffic, what will likely happen?

options.text: You will block traffic and may get a ticket.
You will show good defensive driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will block traffic and may get a ticket.
questions.explanation: You must match the speed of traffic unless traffic is going over the speed limit. Driving too slowly can block traffic and result in a ticket.

questions.question: You see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane. What should you do?

options.text: The pedestrian must yield the right-of-way.
Honk your horn to alert them.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog shows that a pedestrian is blind or partially blind. You must yield the right-of-way to these pedestrians.

questions.question: Fog reduces visibility. When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Drive carefully and reduce your speed.
Not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to see the road better.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: In fog, drive slowly and carefully. Do not use high beams. Use low beams instead—they work better in fog to light up the road and objects ahead.

questions.question: You must park in an unusual spot. What should you do?

options.text: Make sure drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
Park five feet from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
questions.explanation: Your parked vehicle must not become a hazard. Wherever you park, make sure drivers approaching from any direction can see your car.

questions.question: Which drugs can affect your driving?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of these
questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair your driving, including illegal drugs and legal prescription or over-the-counter medicines. Driving impaired by any drug is a crime.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It tells drivers that right turns are not allowed at this location.

questions.question: At an intersection with no traffic signals or stop signs, a driver should:

options.text: Keep going at the same speed.
Stop, look both ways, and then go.
Let all other drivers go first.
Be ready to yield if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield if needed.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, be ready to yield to vehicles coming from the right. Stay alert by releasing the accelerator, covering the brake, and looking left, right, and left again to avoid a crash.

questions.question: You cannot pass on either side of a ____ centerline.
questions.correctAnswerText: Double solid yellow
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no one can cross it to pass. Cars traveling in either direction must stay in their lane.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drugs and driving?

options.text: Any prescription drug is safe if you don't feel drowsy.
Over-the-counter drugs can also affect your driving.
Only illegal drugs affect your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over-the-counter drugs can also affect your driving.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving. This includes drugs for colds, allergies, and anxiety. It is illegal to drive while affected by any drug that impairs your ability to drive safely, whether it is illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter.

questions.question: A railroad crossbuck sign works like a yield sign.
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: A railroad crossbuck sign is a yield sign. You must yield to any trains and railroad equipment.

questions.question: Backing your vehicle is:

options.text: Dangerous if you have a helper.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always dangerous.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see clearly behind your vehicle. Use extra caution when backing up.

questions.question: Taking drugs with alcohol:

options.text: Increases the risk of a crash.
Is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
Does not affect your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs can damage your brain function and impair your driving. Combining alcohol with other drugs increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Assume all drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Right-of-way rules give guidance, but you should not assume you have the right-of-way. Always watch the situation at an intersection. Yield your right-of-way if it prevents a crash.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
Your road crosses a divided highway.
You are on an overpass over a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your road crosses a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that your road crosses a divided highway. A divided highway has two one-way roads separated by a median or guide rail.

questions.question: When driving in rain, you must:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In rain, use your low beam headlights.

questions.question: Drivers must yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road.
If the pedestrian signals you to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians in the street, even if they are crossing against a red light or being careless.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only a blood alcohol level above the legal limit can
Even a small amount of alcohol can
Only a blood alcohol level above 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even a small amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol reduces your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Your driving skills will suffer. No one can drink and drive safely.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance behind large vehicles that block your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?
questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect back at you and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What do some highways use to direct drivers into the proper lanes for turning?

options.text: White lines on the side of the road
White arrows in the middle of the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes
questions.explanation: White arrows in lanes show which lanes to use for going straight or turning.

questions.question: What helps a person recover from drinking alcohol?
questions.correctAnswerText: Only time
questions.explanation: Only time will reduce the effects of alcohol.

questions.question: When passing a large vehicle, a small vehicle driver must be prepared for what?

options.text: Wind gusts from the large vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wind gusts from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create strong wind gusts that can push smaller vehicles sideways. Drivers of small vehicles should be ready to steer correctly when passing large vehicles moving at high speeds.

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?
questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: A round sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead. It is posted a few hundred feet before the tracks. Drivers should slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: If a vehicle skids on water, the driver should quickly apply the brakes.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: If a vehicle hydroplanes, do not slam on the brakes. Instead, release the accelerator and try to regain control. Ride out the skid if you cannot regain control.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on a wet roadway?

options.text: As you drive faster, your tires become less effective.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
As you decrease your speed, the roadway becomes more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: As you drive faster, your tires become less effective.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive on wet roads, the less effective your tires become at removing water. At high speeds, your tires lose grip and you begin to hydroplane—sliding on a film of water.

questions.question: What should you do if oncoming headlights blind you at night?

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch your lights to high beams.
Turn your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights blind you, look at the right edge of the road instead of ahead. This keeps your vehicle on the road until you pass the other car.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Pull over to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle behind you, slow down and safely pull over to the right side of the road. If you are in heavy traffic, keep moving slowly until you can move out of the way.

questions.question: If your car's suspension is bad, what can it cause?
questions.correctAnswerText: Problems controlling your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Your suspension helps you control your vehicle and keeps your ride smooth. If your car bounces a lot after hitting a bump or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: When must you yield for emergency vehicles?

options.text: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles pass when they use sirens or flashing lights.

questions.question: Vehicles behind a school bus with red lights flashing must stay stopped until:

options.text: The stop arm is pulled in.
The stop arm is pulled in and the bus starts moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm is pulled in and the bus starts moving.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights and its stop arm out, you must stay stopped until the lights turn off, the arm is pulled in, and the bus drives again.

questions.question: When you leave a parking spot on the curb and enter traffic, you should:

options.text: Drive slower than other traffic for 200 feet.
Wait for a big enough gap to match the speed of traffic.
Wait for two vehicles to pass, then enter the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a big enough gap to match the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: When you merge into traffic, wait for a gap large enough to speed up to match other vehicles.

questions.question: Two vehicles enter an intersection from different roads at the same time. Which vehicle must yield?
questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left
questions.explanation: At any intersection, when two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street in the wrong direction.
You may go if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are entering a one-way street in the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: If you pass these signs, you are going the wrong way and may crash head-on. Turn around carefully.

questions.question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember that trucks generally:

options.text: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass on a downhill road than smaller vehicles.
Have a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass on an uphill road than smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Because of their size and weight, trucks take longer to stop than smaller vehicles.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
Check only the inside rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder to ensure it is safe.

questions.question: Pedestrians in crosswalks and at intersections always have the right-of-way.
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way when crossing at an intersection, whether the crosswalk is marked or unmarked.

questions.question: A "No stopping" sign means you may only stop if:

options.text: You need to avoid hitting another vehicle.
You stop for less than five minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You need to avoid hitting another vehicle.
questions.explanation: A "No stopping" sign means you can only stop to obey a traffic signal, follow a police officer's directions, or prevent a crash with another vehicle.
